reach.rationale: The app uses only APIs that were already stable before Astro 7; none of the v7-era features (advanced routing, route caching, CDN providers, Vite 8 specifics) are touched. The platform version is current (7.4.4), but the API surface is entirely long-stable.

containment.rationale: There are no experimental APIs to contain; the framework surface is minimal and centralized.

evidence: app/src/lib/pokeapi.ts:28-46 — hand-rolled caching instead of Astro 7's newly-stable route caching, a deliberate low-risk choice
app/package.json:8-9 — deps are exactly the two stable packages needed (astro, @astrojs/node), no beta/RC/canary packages
justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used, so there is nothing unjustified; each stable API used is the plainly idiomatic option.

findings.issue: Exact-pinned versions (astro 7.4.4, @astrojs/node 11.1.9) at the very newest patch of a minor line released 2026-10-15; not experimental, but the pins freeze the app against bugfix releases
findings.suggestion: Use caret ranges (e.g. ^7.4.4) so patch/minor fixes flow in via lockfile updates

findings.issue: A hand-rolled module-level promise cache duplicates work Astro 7 newly stabilized (route caching via cache/routeRules in config), which the app ignores
findings.suggestion: Optional modernization: consider the stable cache/routeRules config in astro.config.mjs for per-route caching instead of the custom Map; the current approach is correct and per-spec, so this is informational

summary: The app is maximally conservative: zero experimental, preview, or recently-unstable APIs, no experimental config flags, and a framework touch limited to long-stable primitives (props, params, url, response, dynamic routes, bundled scripts). It runs on the current stable line (Astro 7.4.x, @astrojs/node 11.1.9) but deliberately avoids even Astro 7's newly-stabilized features. From an experimentalness/risk standpoint there is essentially nothing to flag beyond exact version pins.
